policy: These records are later Stable/GA qualification and Form Package/public-service publication obligations. Open records block publishing the Beta Form Packages, Interface/Binding Definitions as independently published artifacts, and claims of Stable, GA, independent-host, real-backend, or third-party ecosystem readiness. They do not block the stable provider v2.1.1 release from embedding the exactly locked 15 Experimental Beta FormRefs and digests after its local provider gate passes. Closing an obligation still requires the evidence it names; no local gate fabricates independent-host, hosted-operation, real-backend, or third-party evidence. Retained packages and append-only security revocation remain outside this policy.

blockers.title: A real host preserves the exact FormRef
blockers.rationale: The provider dispatches read, update and delete on the ref recorded in state. Until a host outside this repository answers for an exact ref rather than for a kind, that dispatch is unproven against anything but the reference host.

blockers.title: An independent host enforces a relation target's exact contract
blockers.rationale: The portable contract and reference host now require every relation to state exactly one target FormRef or Interface contract and revalidate that requirement before mutation and asynchronous commit (decision 0022). The host stores both the target UID and exact FormRef, and reports contract drift as ExternalChange. This closes the contract-authoring and reference-host implementation gap, but no host outside this repository has yet demonstrated the rule. V3-002 therefore remains open only for independent-host evidence. Its acceptance slice overlaps V3-004's independent Host API evidence, but V3-002 is retained as the relation-specific check that the host enforces the exact target contract.

blockers.title: Runtime loadable media types and artifact manifest media types agree
blockers.rationale: The runtime ABI and the artifact manifest each state a media-type set, and they disagree. A bundle can therefore be accepted by one and unusable by the other.

blockers.title: An independent host implements Host API v1beta1
blockers.rationale: The only implementation of this lane is the disposable reference host inside this repository. A lane with one implementation, written by the same people who wrote the contract, has not shown that its contract is implementable by anyone else.

blockers.title: A real backend materialises and serves the edge application revisions
blockers.rationale: Immutable code and asset revisions, weighted traffic, and transactional ordered SQLite migration history are these Forms' whole value. The reference host proves manifest closure, exact relations, asset fallback preconditions, and the append-only path-and-digest ledger state machine, but it serves no application traffic and executes no SQL. Until a real backend serves the referenced asset bytes with the declared worker ordering and commits each SQL file with its ledger record in one real SQLite transaction, those data-plane effects are asserted rather than demonstrated.

blockers.title: A real backend materialises an edge KV namespace and its typed binding
blockers.rationale: A binding projects an API into a running isolate. Nothing in this repository can prove that projection; only a real runtime can.

blockers.title: A worker is reachable over HTTPS without a customer-owned domain
blockers.rationale: The lane now states the contract: WorkerEndpoint asks for reachability and nothing else, the host assigns the address and publishes it as typed outputs, at most one exists per worker, and it invokes the active deployment's fetch handler. What it does not do is send a request. This lane drives desired state, so it proves that a host answers with a complete HTTPS address it assigned and keeps that address stable across a promotion; it cannot prove that anything is listening on it. The blocker closes on a real backend serving traffic at a host-assigned hostname, not on the Form existing.

blockers.title: A real runtime is measured against the ABI contract
blockers.rationale: The Host API lane proves that a host states which ABI it implements and holds desired state to it. It does not prove that an isolate behaves that way. conformance/runtime-abi-v1 is the corpus that measures one, and its existence is not this blocker closing: what closes it is a passed deployed-runtime-conformance-run, with the module-loader lane measured, against a runtime this repository does not own. A run against the repository's in-process stand-in proves the corpus and never a runtime, and every report says which of the two it is (decision 0023).

blockers.title: A provider lifecycle runs end to end against an independent host
blockers.rationale: Create, roll out, promote, roll back, observe, recover from an interrupted apply, and destroy must be demonstrated as one sequence against a host this repository does not own, because the failure modes worth catching only appear between the steps.

blockers.title: Destroy completes through a real backend and leaves nothing orphaned
blockers.rationale: A platform that cannot reliably delete what it created is not one anybody should adopt. An orphan scan finding nothing, against a real backend, is the evidence.

blockers.title: The ABI declares a tail handler nothing can activate
blockers.rationale: CLOSED by removal. worker.runtime@1.0.0 declared a tail handler no resource in this family could activate — the inward-activation attachments are WorkerCustomDomain (fetch), WorkerCronTrigger (scheduled), QueueConsumer (queue) and WorkerEndpoint (fetch) — so no portable deployment could cause a host to invoke it, no run could observe it, and two hosts could implement it differently with nothing able to detect the divergence. The handler, its maxTailEventsPerBatch limit, the WorkerVersion handlers enum entry, the runtime corpus probe route and fixtures, and the corpus's unmeasured entry are all gone; the vocabulary is fetch, scheduled, queue. The property that replaces it is enforced rather than described: the runtime corpus loader refuses a corpus in which a declared handler has no check measuring it, and an unmeasured entry does not discharge one, so re-adding tail without the attachment that makes it observable fails corpus verification by name. tail returns with that attachment and a new exact worker.runtime version, never as a bare handler (decision 0019).

blockers.title: Resource plane is tenant-isolated
blockers.rationale: A resource's internal address must carry the tenant. Until the contract states that and the corpus drives it, a host may ship an address of space, kind and name — so two tenants naming one resource in one space share one record, one tenant reads, updates and deletes another's, a reference resolves across the boundary and pins a foreign uid, one prepareDigest is spendable by anyone holding it, and one Idempotency-Key replays another tenant's success. This is the single most damaging host defect the lane could permit, and the reference host itself carried the shape of it. The lane now states the rule normatively and measures it with ten black-box checks driven from two configured tenants, nine of them enumerated by surface rather than by intent so that every endpoint taking a resource name — observe and import included — is measured, and the tenth the permissive half none of the nine states: each tenant mutating its own plane, while the holder of a resource a stranger reached for can still update and delete it (spec/decisions/0028). What is NOT closed, and what this blocker is, is the same thing V3-004 is: no host outside this repository has been measured against it. It closes on a passed portable-host-v3 run, including the ten tenant checks, against a host this repository does not own.

blockers.title: A replay record does not outlive the incarnation it reports
blockers.rationale: A create's prepare binds the create markers, so a byte-identical re-create derives a byte-identical Idempotency-Key and fingerprint. Against a host that keeps its replay records forever, terraform destroy followed by terraform apply of an unchanged configuration reports success, creates nothing, and never converges: the next read 404s, the plan proposes the create again, and it replays again. No client can close it, because the discriminator is the deletion the host performed in between; and the determinism must stay, because it is the only answer to a create whose response was lost. The lane now states the host rule in decision 0011 and measures all three of its edges with replay-record-retires-with-its-incarnation. What is NOT closed is the same thing V3-004 and V3-012 are: no host outside this repository has been measured against it. It closes on a passed portable-host-v3 run, including that check, against a host this repository does not own.

blockers.title: A real backend proves an adoption adopts rather than mints
blockers.rationale: import carries a nativeId, and the lane now holds a host to it: one live resource per native identity within a tenant, an immutable recorded claim, released with its holder, spanning every space of the tenant and stopping there (decision 0011, amended). That proves a host BINDS an adoption to the identity it was given and will not manage one backend object twice, which is what fails a host whose /import is a plain create. It does not prove that the object named existed before the call, or that the host did not also mint a fresh one beside it. Neither is reachable from a portable surface: a native identifier is host detail and stays off every response, the published wire documents are closed, and a black-box runner cannot name an object it knows a host already holds without depending on that host's identifier format. It closes on a terraform import against a real backend of an object that backend provisioned out of band, shown afterwards to be the same object rather than a duplicate, with a second import of it refused.
